agent_notes: The registry proposes deity.teraphim (Supernatural). I made them an ARTIFACT because the plot treats them as portable objects (stolen, hidden in a saddlebag, searched for), while Laban calls them 'my gods' (31:30). tipnr_id kept so the registry link survives.
'His brethren' in 31:46 and 31:54 are read as Jacob's kinsmen and retainers; the text does not say who they are. Some commentators think both parties' relatives share the meal at 31:46.
'His brethren' (31:23, 25) are Laban's kinsmen, not necessarily brothers; defined as a group. Not the same entity as group.sons_of_laban.

The registry maps Jegar-sahadutha, Galeed and Mizpah (31:47-49) to Ramoth-gilead (loc.ramoth). That is a different, later city of refuge, so I did not reuse it: loc.galeed is the cairn site in the hill country of Gilead with no tipnr_id and no coordinates (reviewer: place not securely identified; the cairn is traditionally sought east of the Jordan near the Jabbok). Galeed, Jegar-sahadutha and Mizpah are treated as names of one site.

agent_notes: 'By night' (31:24); Laban says 'yesternight' in 31:29, so the dream falls the night before the overtaking. I placed it 6 days after the pursuit started at 22:00 (middle watch), which is the night before the pursuit ends. The exact hour is my choice; the text gives only 'night'.

agent_notes: The text counts 3 days until Laban is told (31:22) and a 7-day pursuit (31:23), so Jacob has travelled about 10 days when overtaken. Paddan to Gilead is about 754 km by road: 23 days by donkey, 41 by army with flocks and children (urim travel). The text wins; the gap is a real tension, which Rashi (31:23) resolves by saying Laban covered in one day what Jacob did in seven. If Laban's flocks were not near Haran but 3 days away (30:36) the count shifts, but not enough to close the gap. The 10-day span is the text's own count (3 + 7), not an estimate from the road; the flight event itself is only the departure day, so that the link to laban_told does not run backwards.
Jacob leaves while Laban is away shearing (31:19). The one-day delay after the council is my estimate; the margin of two days allows for waiting for Laban's departure.

history.note: [consider] Consider adding caus.gen_31.tents_searched.jacob_rebukes_laban (TRIGGERS): the fruitless search of his tents provokes Jacob's rebuke. (GEN.31.35-36: "And he searched, but found not the images. And Jacob was wroth, and chode with Laban".)

agent_notes: Laban 'overtook Jacob' (31:25); the text does not give the hour. The accusation, the search of tents, Jacob's rebuke, the covenant and the meal are put in one continuous day-and-night, with the departure the next morning (31:55). That the covenant meal happens in the evening and the night ('tarried all night', 31:54) is my reading.

Rashi and Rashbam disagree on the 7 days: Rashi says Jacob had a six-day lead and Laban covered it in one day of miracle-speed; Rashbam says Jacob went slowly because of the flocks and Laban caught up at the end of seven days. Both give the pursuit a duration of 7 days; I do not add the 3 days a second time because the 7-day pursuit starts when Laban hears.

Dating by the twenty years in Laban's house (31:38, 41): 14 for the wives (Joseph is born at the end of them, Gen 30:25 'when Rachel had borne Joseph') plus 6 for the flocks (31:41). So the departure falls about 6 years after Joseph's birth, anchored on evt.gen_30.joseph_born END with a margin of a year. This is later than evt.gen_30.jacob_prospers (c. 1913 BCE), which is a state that continues.

notes.note: All 54 verses of the chapter in this corpus are covered. Laban's early-morning departure (English 31:55) is Hebrew 32:1 and falls in the next chapter: the Gen 32 session should anchor it on evt.gen_31.covenant_feast END with BOKER. The dream retold in 31:10-13 (the flocks mating, the angel's call 'return to the land of your kindred') belongs to years earlier, after Laban changed the wages; it is reported inside Jacob's speech to his wives, so it is not a separate event and sits under evt.gen_31.jacob_calls_wives. Its command is the second word fulfilled by the flight; I linked only the explicit Yahweh word of 31:3.

Divine speeches checked: 31:3 (Yahweh: return) is fulfilled by the flight (31:17-21); 31:24 (God to Laban: take heed) is fulfilled in Laban's restraint, which he reports himself in 31:29 and which shows in his speech rather than in a separate event, so I linked it as ENABLES to the accusation. The angel's word of 31:11-13 is the same command as 31:3. Gen 32 (Mahanaim, Jacob's fear of Esau) will be the next chapter; 31:3 'I will be with you' is fulfilled there in part, and the Gen 32 session will write that link.
